_readme: Elton draft. [[c:...]] is cyan = not confirmed. History from the Elton Parish Council short history unless noted.
name: The Crown Inn (finale)

layers.essential_history: [[c:Back where you started. Around a thousand years ago, a Dane called Dacus is said to have bet the whole village in a drinking contest, and Bishop Aethelric had to raise fifty marks of gold overnight to buy it.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The bishop gave the village to Ramsey Abbey when he died in 1034, and the abbey held it for nearly 300 years.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Back at the inn, the Queen's servants, the miller, the ford-keeper and Master Hale are all waiting. Time to say who took the casket.]]

sources.title: Elton Parish Council: A short history of Elton

directions_to_next: [[c:That's the end of the walk. Well done!]]
support: [[c:Support the village: have a drink at the Crown before your walk, or book a table for when you get back.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:Who took the casket?]]
puzzle.intro: [[c:Look through your evidence notebook, then make your accusation.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Who took the casket, why, and where is it hidden?]]

fields.label: Why?
options: To keep it safe for the Queen's family
To sell the jewels in London
To pay off a debt at the inn
fields.answer: To sell the jewels in London

fields.label: Where is it hidden?
options: In a flour sack at the mill
fields.answer: In a flour sack at the mill

hints: [[c:Who crossed the ford twice and said he never left the inn?]]
[[c:What did the torn letter in the post bag say?]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:It was Master Richard Hale. He crossed the ford with the casket, borrowed the mill key and hid it in an extra flour sack by the wheel, so he could sell the Queen's jewels in London. Ned took his shilling, Thomas only lent his key and Mistress Carey tried to help. The casket is found and goes on with the Queen to Peterborough.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:You can solve this from your notebook alone.]]
